chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from some of his companions from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is disliked that a garment be purchased for a dinar that is not a full dirham, because it is not known how much of the dinar the dirham constitutes.

key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: Dirham - a silver coin used as currency
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: Dinar - a gold coin used as currency
key_terms.غَيْرَ دِرْهَمٍ: Not a (full) dirham - referring to a fractional or mixed amount
key_terms.لِأَنَّهُ لَا يُدْرَى: Because it is not known - indicating the reason for the ruling is uncertainty
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh) - a legal ruling indicating preference for avoidance but not strict prohibition

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying goods with a mixed currency amount like one dinar and a fraction of a dirham?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic concern with *gharar* (ambiguity) in currency exchange, specifically prohibiting mixed-currency transactions where the fractional value of the dirham relative to the dinar is not fixed. It reflects the historical context of the Abbasid era when dinars and dirhams circulated with fluctuating exchange rates, necessitating precise valuation to prevent dispute. The ruling underscores the principle that any uncertainty in the quantity or value of the counter-party in a sale invalidates the contract's certainty.
